content.text:
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "assets": [
    {
      "name": "stg_orders",
      "type": "model",
      "description": "One row per source order, including all lifecycle statuses.",
      "owner": "data-platform",
      "lifecycle": "active",
      "grain": ["order_id"],
      "canonical": true
    },
    {
      "name": "customer_orders",
      "type": "model",
      "description": "Completed-order metrics at one row per customer; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.",
      "owner": "analytics",
      "lifecycle": "active",
      "grain": ["customer_id"],
      "canonical": true
    },
    {
      "name": "daily_revenue",
      "type": "model",
      "description": "Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.",
      "owner": "finance-analytics",
      "lifecycle": "active",
      "grain": ["order_date"],
      "canonical": true
    }
  ]
}

version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_orders
    description: One row per source order, including all lifecycle statuses.
    config:
      meta:
        owner: data-platform
        lifecycle: active
        grain: order_id
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        description: Source order identifier.
        data_tests: [not_null, unique]
      - name: customer_id
        description: Customer that placed the order.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: status
        description: Current order lifecycle status.
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [completed, refunded, cancelled]
      - name: order_date
        description: Date the order was placed.
        data_tests: [not_null]

  - name: customer_orders
    description: Completed-order metrics at one row per customer; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.
    config:
      meta:
        owner: analytics
        lifecycle: active
        grain: customer_id
    columns:
      - name: customer_id
        description: Customer identifier and model grain.
        data_tests: [not_null, unique]
      - name: completed_order_count
        description: Number of completed orders for the customer.

  - name: daily_revenue
    description: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.
    config:
      meta:
        owner: finance-analytics
        lifecycle: active
        grain: order_date
    columns:
      - name: order_date
        description: Order date and model grain.
        data_tests: [not_null, unique]
      - name: completed_order_count
        description: Number of completed orders on the date.
      - name: completed_revenue
        description: Sum of completed order amounts on the date.

select
    orders.customer_id,
    orders.order_id,
    items.order_item_id,
    orders.amount
from {{ ref('stg_orders') }} as orders
inner join {{ ref('raw_order_items') }} as items
    on orders.order_id = items.order_id
where orders.status = 'completed'

action.rationale: Confirm whether the order-item detail output is intended or an accidental change to the customer-level metrics model before updating its catalog description or grain.

findings.claim: The SQL now joins stg_orders to raw_order_items and selects order and item identifiers without aggregation, instead of producing completed-order metrics at one row per customer. The catalog and schema still declare customer_id as the grain and describe customer-level metrics.

plan.summary: The proposed customer_orders SQL materially changes its documented customer-level aggregation to order-item-level detail, creating grain and join drift. The change also makes the catalog and schema description and grain metadata inconsistent with the SQL; review is needed before updating metadata because the change may be unintended.
unresolved_questions: Is the intended customer_orders asset still customer-level completed-order metrics, or should the order-item detail output be a separate model?
Can order amounts be repeated across multiple joined item rows, and if so, is that behavior intentional?
